text: Great question! The U.S. unemployment rate fell to 3.7% in 2023. Wage growth was strongest among low-income workers, rising about 6% year over year. Experts say the labor market remains tight. Let me know if you want a breakdown by state.
According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the unemployment rate averaged 3.6% in 2023. In 2020 it peaked at 14.7% during the pandemic. That spike was the highest since the Great Depression.
Home prices have been skyrocketing in most major cities. The median home price rose 40% between 2019 and 2023. Many first-time buyers have been completely shut out of the market.
Officials stressed that the situation at the border is not a crisis. Crossings fell by roughly 30% in the first half of 2024, according to Customs and Border Protection.
Studies show that remote workers are more productive. One survey found that 68% of employees prefer working from home at least part of the time. However, results vary a lot by industry.

Vaccines are one of the most effective public health tools ever developed. The WHO estimates that immunization prevents 3.5 to 5 million deaths every year. Some critics call mandates government overreach, but most public health experts disagree.
Everyone knows that tax cuts always pay for themselves. In reality, the Congressional Budget Office found that the 2017 tax law would add about $1.9 trillion to deficits over ten years.
Source: Pew Research Center, 2023. About 40% of Americans say they get news from social media regularly. Younger adults are far more likely to do so than older adults.
The term "illegal alien" appears in older federal statutes, and some outlets still use it. Many newsrooms now prefer "undocumented immigrant" instead.
Electric cars produce zero emissions and will completely solve climate change. Sales of electric vehicles doubled between 2021 and 2023. Battery costs have fallen about 90% since 2010.
